title: Addressing Correlated Latent Exogenous Variables in Debiased Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Selection bias in recommender-system interactions distorts representations of user preferences and hinders recommendation accuracy and fairness.

gap.claim: From a structural causal model perspective, previous recommender-system debiasing methods assume independent exogenous variables.

contributions.claim: A likelihood-maximization learning algorithm is proposed without assuming independent exogenous variables.
A unified method is proposed to handle latent exogenous variables, including discussion of its relationship to unmeasured confounding.
The data-generation process is modeled with latent exogenous variables under mild normality assumptions, and a Monte Carlo algorithm is developed to estimate the likelihood numerically.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on synthetic datasets and three real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, according to the authors.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommender systems seek personalized content but face selection bias because users interact only with preferred items.
Selection bias distorts user-preference representations and harms recommendation accuracy and fairness.
Existing debiasing approaches include error imputation, inverse propensity scoring, and doubly robust techniques, but structurally assume independent exogenous variables.
The paper proposes likelihood-based learning, a unified treatment of latent exogenous variables, a latent-variable data-generation model, and Monte Carlo likelihood estimation.
The authors report experiments on synthetic and three real-world datasets and provide code.

source_observation.claim: The proposed approach models correlated latent exogenous variables and estimates its likelihood with Monte Carlo computation.

interpretation.claim: Debiasing methods may need to represent dependence among latent causes rather than assume exogenous independence.

application.claim: When applying causal debiasing to recommender systems, evaluate whether latent exogenous variables may be correlated and choose a likelihood-estimation strategy compatible with that structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that correlated latent exogenous variables occur in every recommender-system setting or that the method is preferable under all data-generating conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative experimental results.
The abstract does not describe the theoretical guarantees, optimization details, computational cost, or limitations.
